evidence: The exact nsjail env builders validate each key before adding it to the subprocess environment and --env argv; the standalone validator also admits one final LF because it uses Python match with $, so the contract covers only the no-equals separator property.
adoption.rationale: This narrow source-backed property checks that the regex keeps the POSIX name/value delimiter out of environment-variable names before the nsjail subprocess handoff. It provides a regression gate for the sandbox configuration boundary without claiming that all accepted names are fully POSIX compliant, that the unsafe PID fallback is covered, or that a current security impact exists.

contract.declared_domain: All Python str environment-variable keys passed to the pinned NsjailExecutor._validate_env_key call sites, with no length bound. The exact Python match language includes ASCII identifiers and may also admit one final LF because of '$'. The guarantee is only that an admitted key contains no '='; it does not claim complete POSIX-name validity or behavior in the unsafe PID fallback.
contract.guarantee: Every key accepted by the exact pinned _ENV_VAR_KEY_PATTERN.match call contains no '='. This prevents a key from crossing the name/value separator in a POSIX name=value environment entry and keeps such a key out of the nsjail --env name arguments. No complete POSIX identifier, environment-value, sandbox-isolation, vulnerability, or deployed-impact claim is made.
contract.input_source: For core.script.run_python, user-authored workflow action args.env_vars are read from evaluated_args, merged with Tracecat SDK context, and passed to SandboxService.run_python. When nsjail is available, NsjailExecutor._build_env_map validates each non-PYTHONPATH key before inserting it into the child environment and constructing --env arguments. Registry-action SDK context keys also pass through _build_action_env_map and the same validator. Direct/unsafe PID fallback behavior is outside this contract.
